<!-- Generated by docs-infra Python API -->

```python
build(fwd: Callable, config: ModelConfig, *, seq_len: int | None = None, batch_size: int | None = None, backend: object = None, device: object = None, cache: object = None, pack_weights: bool | None = None, family: str | None = None, **options: object) -> 'evoxc.Executable'
```

Part of [`evoxc_hf.pipeline`](/api/evoxc-hf/pipeline/)

Also available as `evoxc_hf.build`.

Build (trace → lower → compile → load) the executable of one forward.

The whole forward pass becomes **one** compiled graph whose weights are
ordinary graph inputs (`evoxc_hf.param_specs`) and whose `input_ids` is
a `(batch_size, seq_len)` `evoxc.int32` input. All shapes are static: a
different `seq_len`/`batch_size` is a different graph.

`seq_len`/`batch_size`/`pack_weights` normally come from `fwd`
itself: `evoxc_hf.forward_fn` stamps its static specialisation on the
forward, so `build(forward_fn(config, seq_len=8), config)` builds the id
spec that graph actually has. An explicit value that *disagrees* with the
forward is an error (never a silently mismatched ids spec); an omitted one is
taken from the forward, falling back to
`evoxc_hf.resolve_seq_len`/1/`False` for an unstamped forward.

Calls are memoised: the graph is a pure function of `(family, config,
seq_len, batch_size, pack_weights)` — `evoxc_hf.forward_fn` returns the
same object for the same specialisation — so two identical calls return the
**same** `Executable` object and no second compile happens. Backend/device/
options participate in evoxc's cache key, so changing any of them is a new
artifact. Weight identity deliberately does **not** (see the module
docstring).

## Parameters

- `fwd` · `Callable` — the `@evoxc.defn` forward to stage — the object returned by
  `evoxc_hf.forward_fn` (its specialisation is read from it).

- `config` · `ModelConfig` — the model config — a static specialisation value (one config =
  one graph).

- `seq_len` · `int | None` — static sequence length; `1 <= seq_len <=
  config.max_position_embeddings`. `None` (default) takes the
  forward's own length.

- `batch_size` · `int | None` — static batch size. `None` (default) takes the forward's own
  batch size (1 when it has none).

- `backend` · `object` — `None` (resolve the documented default matrix, see
  `resolve_build_options`), a backend name (`"numpy"`,
  `"iree"`, `"xla"`, `"tvm"` …) or an evoxc backend instance.

- `device` · `object` — `None` or an `evoxc.core.Device` the executable should run
  on.

- `cache` · `object` — an `evoxc.CompileCache` to memoise into, or `None` for the
  process-wide default cache.

- `pack_weights` · `bool | None` — opt-in **packed weights**. `True` means the forward takes
  a handful of concatenated params inputs
  (`evoxc_hf.pack.PackPlan.specs`) instead of one input per
  canonical weight; it must match the forward (`None`, the default,
  takes the forward's own mode). This is what makes the 124M-model case
  runnable on IREE (its runtime SIGSEGVs above ~161 consumed inputs;
  `gpt2` declares 197 unpacked). Run it with the packed tree —
  `evoxc_hf.pack_params` — never with the canonical tree.

- `family` · `str | None` — optional explicit family key; when given it must agree with
  `config.family`.

- `**options` · `object` — compile options forwarded to `evoxc.build_cached` (and hence
  to both `lower` and `compile` — that is what makes
  `iree_compile_args` effective). Explicit values always beat the
  injected defaults.

## Returns

- `'evoxc.Executable'` — evoxc.Executable: the loaded executable; call it with a params mapping and integer `input_ids` through `run` / `evoxc.run`. For `pack_weights=True` that mapping is the packed tree.

## Raises

- `HFConfigError` — `seq_len`/`batch_size` is not a positive integer,
  `seq_len` exceeds `config.max_position_embeddings`, `family`
  disagrees with `config.family`, or an explicit
  `seq_len`/`batch_size`/`pack_weights` disagrees with the
  forward's own specialisation.

- `HFUnsupportedError` — unknown `family`, unsupported `config.hidden_act`,
  an erf-based activation on a compiled backend (raised before any
  tracing), or a non-static config shape that cannot be packed.

- `TypeError` — `config` is not a `~evoxc_hf.config.ModelConfig`, or
  `fwd` is not `@evoxc.defn`-marked (build one with
  `evoxc_hf.forward_fn`), or `pack_weights` is not a bool.

- `evoxc.BackendError` — the resolved backend is unavailable or rejects the
  graph (propagated verbatim — never a silent fallback).
